tweets.text:
Tesla is built different. Yesterday my dad and I attended a big opening party in Plano, TX for the newest area Service Center and Gallery. 

Among the many displays and activities, they had an "Ask a Tech" table set up where you could, well, ask a tech. 

My Dad had been having a GPS Accuracy issue with his Model Y for the past few weeks, so we spoke with these gentlemen about it. 

After the tech explained some GPS basics such as antenna location and calibration, he asked if my Dad had anything attached to his USB ports. 

My Dad had just added another hub recently (he loves to have a million devices) and thought the issue may have started around that time. 

Apparently, an unshielded USB accessory can cause interference with the GPS system, among other things. 

The tech suggested disconnecting the USB accessories and performing a soft two-button reset. Sure enough, it worked and the GPS accuracy issue was fixed.

They also had stations for DIY demos for wiper changes, air filters, and detailing in addition to vehicle demos, food, and adoptable dogs from a local pet shelter. 

We saw a small light show, petted some dogs, drove a Cybertruck, talked to lots of awesome employees, and had a great time. 

And best of all we avoided a service visit for what ended up being a simple but perplexing GPS issue. Time well spent!
